subject.title: fix: normalize unsupported Anthropic inline images

question: Should Anthropic inline-image normalization become an optional `AiTransportHost` capability, or must the behavior live entirely in an existing core media/sanitizer boundary?
rationale: Both approaches can fix the bug, but introducing a provider-specific host capability establishes a long-lived API and ownership precedent that correctness tests cannot decide.

options.title: Approve the host capability
options.body: Accept the optional, source-compatible port because the packaged provider needs host-owned image processing without importing core media code.

options.title: Use the media boundary
options.body: Require normalization at the existing sanitizer seam and prove that every packaged-provider and custom-transport user and tool-result path passes through it.

recommendation.title: Approve the host capability
recommendation.body: Accept the optional, source-compatible port because the packaged provider needs host-owned image processing without importing core media code.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a decision about the permanent public-package and core ownership boundary.
